lines.text: Phase six, lesson T24: meet XORA. Time to see the app that does the checking with you.
XORA is an app that watches crypto coins, finds trade setups and helps you manage trades.
Behind it is one engine. It runs in three account modes: Demo, Live and Live Support.
Demo uses simulated fills: no real money. Live sends real Binance futures orders. Live Support only alerts you.
Demo is the default. Start there, like a pilot in a flight simulator.
Five tabs sit along the bottom: Home, Signals, XORA in the centre, Trades and Settings.
Home is your overview. Signals is for studying a coin. XORA manages an open trade.
Trades is your history. Settings holds your rules.
Home first. At the top: a countdown to the next engine check, and setups waiting.
A pill shows DEMO or LIVE. Then the Bitcoin card, today's result, open P&L and trades in use.
Your coins show a status: in trade, buy, sell, cooldown or watching. All numbers are fictional.
Signals is where you read one coin. Pick up to 20 coins yourself, or use Xora AI coin selection.
Each coin has a price chart, a trade opportunity card, and an entry checklist: a tick or cross per check.
Two buttons stay at the bottom: BUY / LONG and SHORT / SELL, for your own manual orders.
The XORA tab is the control room for an open trade: entry, leverage, margin, and the risk zone, the stop.
Unrealised P&L moves with price. The trailing stop can follow price and lock in some profit.
If you want out, CLOSE POSITION ends the trade yourself, at any time.
Trades shows My Trades: an overview, the full list, and insights. Losing trades are listed too.
Settings holds Binance Connect, Trade Settings, Notifications and About.
Here is the workflow XORA supports.
One: choose coins, or use Xora AI coin selection. Two: read a coin on Signals.
Three: a setup triggers. Four: approve it, place your own BUY or SHORT, or simply skip it.
Five: manage the open trade on the XORA tab. Six: review it later in Trades.
Auto trade approval is off by default. A triggered setup then waits for you to tap Approve.
The approval has a short timer. If you do nothing, it expires and no trade is opened.
On a manual order, the sheet tells you if the engine agrees, or if this one is your call.
Trade Settings are your rules: capital per trade, leverage, concurrent trades, coin selection and more.
Example: 3 USDT margin at 10x leverage controls a 30 USDT position. Leverage magnifies losses too.
With 2 concurrent trades, up to 60 USDT of positions can be open at once. Fictional example.
Now the safety settings. Every trade gets a stop. If a stop cannot be placed, the trade is closed.
Concurrent trades caps open trades, one per coin. A daily stop loss pauses new entries until 00:00 IST.
For Live, use an API key with futures trading on and withdrawals disabled. The secret is stored encrypted.
A common mistake: switching to Live on day one with high leverage, because the app looks smart.
Better: practise in Demo first, keep leverage low, and treat every setup as a maybe, not a promise.
Your turn. Auto trade approval is off, and a setup triggers. What happens next?
It waits for your Approve. If you don't approve before it expires, no trade is opened.
Know the limits. XORA is a tool, not a guarantee. Setups can fail, and stops can slip in fast markets.
In Live, losses are real money, and leverage makes them bigger. Fees come out of every trade.
XORA does not guarantee profits. Demo first. This is not financial advice.
Recap. One engine, three modes, and Demo is where you start.
Five tabs, one workflow: coins, Signals, a setup, your approval, the XORA tab, then Trades.
And safety first: a stop on every trade, a daily stop loss, and withdrawals off on your API key.
